name: two photo cards hard-cut past, each with a ghosted word naming the subject
looks: A rounded card holds a labelled photograph with a short caption pill, and a single huge word ghosted faintly beneath it, naming the subject in oversized type for scale and mood. It hard-cuts to a near-identical card: a different photo, a different caption, a different ghost word.
build: ghost-glyph-headline-card: the ghost word is one oversized line of type at low opacity (12-18%), scaled several times the caption's size, sitting behind/under the photo rather than beside it; the card hard-cuts to the next with the same layout and rhythm, no crossfade, only the photo and the two short text elements changing.
sound: A dry tick on each card's arrival, nothing under the hold.
prompt: Show two or three near-identical photo cards hard-cutting one after another, each with a short caption and one huge word naming its subject ghosted faintly beneath the image, same layout and rhythm every time, so the set reads as a small catalogue of reference subjects.
